description:
I'm a student and passionate developer with a strong focus on building custom Telegram bots. I am deeply fascinated by observational astronomy and space science.

I am developing SKYDAR for the hackathon - a project designed to bring the night sky closer to everyone. SKYDAR combines automated Telegram push notifications for notable celestial events with an interactive sky-mapping web application that guides users on where to look in real time using NASA data and APIs.
summary: SKYDAR turns telescope data into events people can actually go and see. Most tools show dry changes between telescope images. SKYDAR puts NASA SPHEREx observations on a first-person sky map, where glowing dots mark what changed: a spot that moved (brown dwarfs, nearby stars, asteroids), a variable star that brightened, or new data that arrived. For each event it tells you, in plain language, when and where to look from your own location. The web app (also a Telegram Mini App) lets anyone enter RA/Dec, choose a field of view and detector, and play a time-lapse of SPHEREx images, with blink, swipe, subtract/add, co-added bands, on-the-fly spectra, Gaia/WISE overlays, and image quality flags. A Telegram bot sends alerts with a time-lapse GIF. Every view can be opened and embedded by URL. A Demo/Real switch and honest error messages keep it usable when archives are busy. Developed with the help of Claude (an SI tool).
details:
WHAT IT DOES

SKYDAR is a public web app (also a Telegram Mini App) that makes NASA SPHEREx observations understandable to anyone. Instead of tables and raw images, you stand on the ground in a first-person sky map, tap a star or any spot, and watch that patch of sky change over time. Changes found in the data become events - a spot that moved, a variable star that brightened, new data in the archive, a known asteroid passing through - shown as glowing points on the map and in an event feed, with plain-language text and "when and where to look" from your own location (Sun-aware visibility).

HOW IT ADDRESSES THE CHALLENGE

- Enter RA/Dec (degrees or sexagesimal), choose the field of view (0.05-0.5 deg) and the detector (D1-D6), and play a time-lapse of SPHEREx spectral-image cutouts from IRSA, with blink, swipe, subtract (A-B), add (A+B) and an automatic difference layer.

- SPHEREx wavelength changes across the detector, so only frames of the same wavelength are compared; alternatively all bands of a detector can be co-added for better signal-to-noise.

- Spectra are generated on the fly by clicking any position.

- Gaia DR3 (moved to the current epoch with proper motions) and AllWISE overlays; per-frame quality-flag metadata.

- Every view is controlled by URL parameters (ra, dec, fov, det, ...), so it can be embedded elsewhere.

- New data is picked up automatically: frames are queried live from IRSA, and the bot re-checks on a schedule.

- The challenge's test targets (WISE 0855, Barnard's Star, eps Indi B, RW Aur, R Dra) are one-tap "missions".

BEYOND THE CHALLENGE

A Telegram bot sends alerts with a time-lapse GIF and a "when/where to look" line, with subscriptions and no duplicate notifications. Gyroscope mode turns a phone into a window onto the sky. A Demo/Real data switch and honest, specific error messages (e.g. "archive error 503") with saved-data fallbacks keep the tool usable when archives are busy.

IMPACT

Turning dry changes in telescope images into things people can act on invites non-experts into discovery, in the spirit of citizen-science projects such as Backyard Worlds.

TOOLS

Python, FastAPI, NumPy, SciPy, Astropy, PyVO, reproject, Pillow, aiogram, APScheduler; vanilla JavaScript and HTML canvas; Telegram Mini Apps. Data: NASA/IPAC IRSA (SPHEREx, AllWISE), ESA Gaia, d3-celestial star data, IMCCE SkyBoT.

HONEST LIMITS

Results are candidates, not discoveries: no artefact masking and no full cross-match with other catalogues. A SPHEREx pixel is about 6 arcsec, so slow motions need long baselines. Demo mode uses synthetic data and is labelled DEMO. eal mode was tested with live IRSA data on November 15, 2026.

USE OF SI

Developed with Claude (Anthropic): code, interface text and documentation. The developer set the goals, tested the result and chose what to keep. Every source file has a header comment stating this and the README contains a disclosure. The built-in list of 115 stars and fun facts was written by the AI from general knowledge (approximate); the full star catalogue comes from d3-celestial. image of team and a promo video in the end was genereted with SI.

During video recording and final checks, requests to IRSA (for frame retrieval) and Gaia timed out; this occurred on two different networks. The system worked with real data previously; the video displays frames from the local cache. A "Demo" mode has been retained as a fallback; it is marked with a "DEMO" label.

LINKS

Live app: https://skydar-n.onrender.com (only DEMO data)
